question: An engineer must configure a Nexus 7000 series switch for HSRP on VLAN 100. When fully functional, the router must be the active master. Which set of commands must be used to implement the scenario?
options: feature hsrp / interface vlan100 / ip address 10.1.1.2 255.255.255.0 / priority 255 preempt / hsrp version 2 / hsrp 1000 / ip 10.1.1.1
feature-set hsrp / interface vlan100 / ip address 10.1.1.2 255.255.255.0 / priority 20 preempt / hsrp version 2 / hsrp 1000 / ip 10.1.1.1
feature-set hsrp / interface vlan100 / ip address 10.1.1.2 255.255.255.0 / priority 80 preempt / hsrp version 2 / hsrp 1000 / ip 10.1.1.1
feature hsrp / interface vlan100 / ip address 10.1.1.2 255.255.255.0 / priority 240 preempt / hsrp version 2 / hsrp 1000 / ip 10.1.1.1
theory: HSRP determines the active router by comparing configured priority (default 100, higher wins) and, because HSRP does not preempt by default, an already-active lower-priority router will keep its role even if a higher-priority router later comes online — unless "preempt" is explicitly configured. To guarantee this router becomes and stays the active master whenever it's fully functional, it needs both a priority above the default (255, the maximum) and the "preempt" keyword, alongside enabling the feature and assigning the virtual IP under HSRP version 2 group 1000. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 1 — HSRP Priority and Preemption)
